problem: Text and screenshot consent prompts persisted a late Yes even after the parent was closed or destroyed.
change: Reject consent entry and returned answers when a supplied parent is invalid or hidden. Parentless calls remain supported.

reproduction.cases: Text and capture consent after parent rejection, with or without destruction.
reproduction.observed: Consent returned True and attempted a settings write after parent closure.

coverage: Four closure cases return False, preserve consent flags and perform no settings writes or repeated prompts.
Both consent types support No, reopening, Yes and reuse of existing consent, without changing the other permission.
Four real ToolsSettingUI caller cases preserve the previous result and neither present a result nor retry after parent closure or destruction.
Four live caller cases verify that No presents the original result once and Yes retries the original request once.

limitations: Offscreen Qt with substituted message-box answers and settings writes. These new tests send no data.
The existing related TLS test opens a loopback listener; the full selected suite is not a no-network test.
Full regression, independent review and integration remain pending. Native evidence does not cover OS keyboard input, real OCR or a cloud provider request.

caller_fix.observed: ToolsSettingUI still presented the consent-required result after closure, even though the consent helper returned False.
caller_fix.change: After consent returns, stop processing if the tools page is invalid, hidden or its lifetime no longer accepts work. Local results without consent retain their existing path.

native.platform: Windows private desktop, Traditional_Chinese, dark, 900x740 main window
native.entry: Actual tools page callback and consent helpers create real QMessageBox dialogs. No/Yes use widget-local Tab/Space. Closure cases close the tools page and force a late Yes through QMessageBox.done.
native.substitutions: read_result_async records synthetic requests without provider execution; result presentation is recorded. Settings writes use the real writer in an isolated temporary settings directory.
